newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stock market closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African stock market closing report.

text.p: South African shares ended strong on Tuesday with volumes at a record high boosted by a massive trade in NBS Holdings Ltd during the afternoon, dealers said.
"The talk of the day has been the NBS transaction," Johan Marais, director at Societe General Frankel Pollak told Reuters.

The transaction which saw 18 million shares worth 1.357 billion rand moved through the market at 1328 GMT related to the sale by RMB Holdings' of its 22.2 percent stake in NBS to financial group Board of Executors Ltd.
The deal, which was announced in March, drove NBS shares to a new high of 83 rand on Tuesday.

The JSE said in a statement the day's turnover of 2.171 billion rands worth was the highest in its 109-year history. It was also the second consecutive record day of turnover beating Friday's high 1.506 billion rand.
The JSE was closed on Monday for the Freedom Day public holiday.

Dealers said industrial shares had been languishing in negative to flat for much of the day until it received a shot in the arm from the release of U.S. first quarter employment and March durable goods data -- both which showed tame inflationary prospects.
South Africa's industrial index ended up 45.4 points to 8,451.4 and the all-share index added 34.4 points to 7,106.4 points.
The banking an financial sector also saw good trade with the financial index ending up 103.6 points at a fresh record high of 8,905.8 points.

FNB was up 100 cents to 32 rand, Liberty Life added 275 cents to 124.50 rand and RMB shares were also up 70 cents, or 6.48 percent, to 11.50 rand but dealers said the move was unrelated to the NBS transaction.
Gold shares were sickly, depressed by a weak bullion price which has lost $3 since Friday.
The index ended down 29.8 points at another fresh low of 1,205.2 points -- its lowest level since April 1993.
Vaal Reefs dropped 13 rand to 269 rand, Kloof shed 90 cents to 31 rand and Western Deep cut 475 cents to 112.25 rand.
Dealers said volumes on the bourse, excluding the NBS transaction, were thin.
Stocks were seen firm on Wednesday if Wall Street held its early gains until the end, they said.

Near-dated share futures also ended mixed with industrial contracts boosted by the U.S. S&P futures which rose after the release of U.S. first quarter employment index and the March durables, dealers said.
Gold contracts were soft on a sickly bullion price.
The June all-share contract was at 6,580/602 from 6,548, the industrial contract was at 8,313/20 from 8,226 and the gold contract was at 835/44 from 881.
